plain: Giving in meekly to the will of others

webster.text: Yielding to the will or power of another; obedient.

more.text: Humble; acknowledging one's inferiority; testifying one's submission.

example.quote: They have been represented as factious, seditious, and inclined to democracy whenever they have refused passive obedience to provincial mandates as arbitrary as those of Turkish bashaw I say provincial mandates, for to the King and Parliament they have been ever submissive and obedient.
example.cite: James Otis, The Rights of the British Colonies Asserted and Proved (Boston, 1764)
